# Preregistered synthetic local model evaluation corpus

All `.trace` files in this directory are hand-authored synthetic `strace` data. They are not captures from a user's computer. The `/usr/bin/synthetic-*` names are inert data, and `203.0.113.8` is a documentation-only address.

`corpus.json` version 4 preregisters 51 semantic question/case rows, including 15 answerable natural-language variations, 12 unanswerable questions, three four-way source-order groups, and the acceptance criteria before inference. Expected answers are semantic criteria over typed facts, not hard-coded evidence IDs. For each preview the evaluator resolves those criteria against the exact model-preview facts and confirms that the matched records have evidence IDs in the deterministic summary. Targets must resolve uniquely unless a duplicate-target case explicitly permits equivalent matches; ambiguous or missing corpus targets stop evaluation.

Coverage includes direct lookup and more conceptual syscall/outcome questions, errno lookup, exact paths and prefix collisions, omitted path hints, process caller/child relations, duplicate targets, unsupported root-cause questions, wrong syscall/outcome and errno abstentions, partial parses, and source-order permutations. The output schema exposes every bounded evidence ID to the model regardless of question wording. It does not preselect expected evidence or force an abstention. Four traces with the same facts in different source orders are evaluated for each required permutation group.

The deterministic comparator sees the same complete typed facts as the model. It uses declared lexical rules for syscall names, outcomes, errno phrases, exact path strings, and direct caller/child IDs. It selects only a unique highest-scoring fact and abstains on no match or a tie. This transparent lexical baseline is not a learned model or an oracle. The model is useful only if the complete model-plus-validation path beats this baseline on the preregistered set without false selections on unanswerable cases.

The gate requires schema/pin-valid output for every case, at least a 10 percentage-point answerable-accuracy gain over the comparator, zero false selections on unanswerable cases, correct selection on every case in each four-way permutation group, and p95 inference latency no greater than 30 seconds. The evaluator pins the corpus SHA-256, criteria, group sizes, and case count before accepting a run. Memory is not reported as a measured benchmark: the runtime applies a 2 GiB address-space limit, and no peak-RSS result is claimed. Passing a synthetic gate alone does not establish real-world accuracy or justify a safety claim.

The report keeps invalid runs separate from valid abstentions. It reports schema/pin-valid output rate, exact and answerable accuracy, false-selection rate on valid unanswerable cases, baseline measures, permutation correctness, and wall time. Corpus metadata is capped at 64 KiB and 128 cases; child stdout/stderr are individually capped at 1 MiB; each subprocess is timed. Timeouts and malformed or contract-invalid output count as invalid runs, never as empty selections. Inference remains opt-in: each case requires a fresh exact-preview digest confirmation; the helper does not download models or access the network.
